faq: From the Moon's mean synodic cycle (29.53 days) counted from a known new moon — accurate to within hours for planning; almanac-grade instants come from full orbital ephemerides.
What time is the full moon, exactly?
The calculator reports the approximate instant; the Moon looks equally full across the surrounding night, which is the honest precision for viewing plans.
Why does it rise at sunset?
Geometry: a full moon sits opposite the Sun, so it crosses the sky all night — rising as the Sun sets and setting as it rises.
The popular name for the second full moon inside one calendar month — possible because 29.53 days is shorter than most months.
Full moons near perigee look slightly larger (up to ~14% wider than at apogee). The date is the same; the size flourish is orbital, and the calculator's job is the date.
Does the full moon affect tides?
Yes — sun and Moon align, so high tides run higher and low tides lower (spring tides) within a day or so of full and new moons.
Can I look up a past full moon?
Enter a past date and the calculator finds the next full moon after it — the cycle runs both directions.
